differences.sourceBehavior: Retained JavaScript service references remain callable and return old values after provider removal or replacement.
differences.tessivumBehavior: Operations through old generation handles fail with StaleServiceHandle after provider removal or replacement; fresh lookups observe the current provider.
differences.rationale: User explicitly approved retaining Rust generation safety rather than allowing revoked handles to access obsolete services.
differences.conformanceImpact: Rust PASS and upstream TRACE_MISMATCH remain visible for old-reference operations only; consumer readiness, cleanup, and fresh service values must still agree.

differences.sourceBehavior: First activation after a pending config update uses the old expression and retains a removed field.
differences.tessivumBehavior: First activation resolves the latest committed source configuration; whole-config replacement removes obsolete fields.
differences.rationale: User explicitly approved latest-config semantics instead of reproducing stale upstream configuration.
differences.conformanceImpact: Rust PASS and upstream TRACE_MISMATCH remain visible. This approval covers only the first-activation pending-config difference, not other C1 gaps.

differences.sourceBehavior: Cordis and JavaScript consumers may observe Proxy traps and prototype-based object behavior.
differences.tessivumBehavior: Tessivum uses explicit Rust values, handles, and APIs; it does not reproduce JavaScript Proxy or prototype semantics.
differences.rationale: Proxy traps and prototype identity are JavaScript implementation mechanics, not portable core lifecycle behavior.
differences.conformanceImpact: No lifecycle trace difference is permitted.
differences.m0Treatment: Documented only; supported M0 fixtures compare lifecycle behavior, not JavaScript object mechanics.

differences.sourceBehavior: Legacy configuration can contain arbitrary !!js subtrees evaluated by JavaScript.
differences.tessivumBehavior: Tessivum accepts a constrained, deterministic safe-expression language instead of evaluating arbitrary !!js in the Rust host.
differences.rationale: Arbitrary host JavaScript evaluation is neither a safe nor a language-neutral configuration contract.
differences.conformanceImpact: No lifecycle trace difference is permitted; configuration execution is outside M0.
differences.m0Treatment: Loader scenarios return UNSUPPORTED_SCENARIO. Future unsupported legacy !!js input is routed to the Legacy Node Loader rather than evaluated by Rust.
